server.name: StaticSight
server.instructions: StaticSight gives you zero-compile, high-fidelity evidence about an uncompiled C++ repository (Universal Ctags, GNU Global, ripgrep, cppcheck, git, a code graph and local semantic search). For a code review, start with review_changes (one-call bundle) or get_diff_scopes, then drill down with the other tools. Before editing, plan_change maps every place to touch; after each edit, check_my_edit checks it. get_impact, get_call_paths and find_entry_paths follow calls several levels deep; get_context_pack gives everything about one function in one call. Findings carry IDs (F1a2b3c): run verify_finding before reporting one. Truncated lists end with a get_more token. Every result is concise Markdown with file:line references you can cite. Results marked 'heuristic' come from text analysis, not a compiler: verify before asserting.

tools.name: review_changes
tools.description: START HERE for 'review my changes' / 'what could break?'. One-call C++ review bundle for the current branch (committed + staged + unstaged + untracked vs the merge-base with origin/main, falling back to origin/master). Runs, within a token budget: diff scopes, cppcheck on changed files, branch skeletons of changed functions, caller impact of changed functions, memory-layout risks of changed structs, include blast radius of changed headers, lock-consistency checks on members touched by the diff, and lock-order (deadlock) checks for locks the changed functions take. Ends with a reviewer checklist. Use the individual tools afterwards to drill into any item.

params.name: base_ref
params.description: Git ref to diff against. Empty = merge-base with origin/main (fallback origin/master, main, master, HEAD).

params.name: max_symbols
params.description: Maximum number of changed functions/types to analyse in depth.

tools.name: check_my_edit
tools.description: Fast self-check of your own uncommitted C++ edits, meant to run after every edit: for each function changed since the previous check (baseline="last", the default) or since HEAD (baseline="HEAD"), it looks for exit paths that leak what the function allocates, cppcheck errors on the changed lines, callers outside the change that still use an old signature, switches missing a value of an enum the change uses, and platform twins that were not changed. Findings get IDs for `verify_finding`. Use while coding; use `review_changes` for the full review before committing.

params.name: baseline
params.description: 'last' (changes since the previous check_my_edit call) or 'HEAD' (all uncommitted changes).

tools.name: plan_change
tools.description: Plans a change to one function before you edit it: an ordered checklist of every place to touch (definition, declarations, overrides, call sites grouped by file, platform or naming counterparts, header includers), the tests that reach it, its contract, and risks (earlier fixes on these lines, locks it takes, callers that ignore its result). Describe the change in `change` (e.g. "add a timeout parameter"): signature words turn call-site checks into required updates. Use before a refactor or any edit whose ripple you have not mapped yet.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name, optionally qualified (`Class::method`, `ns::fn`), e.g. 'process_packet'.

params.name: change
params.description: Optional short description of the intended change, e.g. 'add a timeout parameter'.

tools.name: get_diff_scopes
tools.description: Maps every changed line of the current diff to the exact C++ function, method, class, struct, enum or macro that encloses it (via Universal Ctags). Also reports new and removed symbols, signature changes (old -> new), struct/class layout changes, header changes, deleted/renamed files, and suggests the next tool calls. Use this first to learn WHAT changed before asking who is affected.

params.name: base_ref
params.description: Git ref to diff against. Empty = merge-base with origin/main (fallback origin/master, main, master, HEAD).

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

tools.name: get_enclosing_scope
tools.description: Returns the innermost C++ function/method/class/struct/namespace that encloses a given line, with its qualified name, signature, parent scope, line range and the line-numbered source (the target line is marked with >). Use when you have a file:line (from a diff, stack trace, or another tool) and need the full surrounding code without reading the whole file.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path relative to the workspace root (absolute paths inside the workspace are accepted).

params.name: target_line
params.description: 1-based line number.

tools.name: get_branch_skeleton
tools.description: Returns only the control-flow skeleton of a C++ function (if/else/switch/case/for/while/do/try/catch/return/throw/break/continue/goto) as an indented tree, annotated with lock acquisitions, allocations/releases, early exits that may leak a resource, and lines changed in the current diff. Use to audit logic paths, error handling and resource pairing cheaply instead of reading the full body. Select the function by symbol name, by start_line (enclosing function), or by an explicit start_line..end_line range.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path relative to the workspace root.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name in that file, e.g. 'process_packet' or 'Router::process_packet'.

params.name: start_line
params.description: 1-based start line. Alone: the enclosing function of this line is used.

params.name: end_line
params.description: 1-based inclusive end line (optional).

tools.name: get_context_pack
tools.description: Everything an agent needs about one function in a single call, within a character budget: location and signature, the documented contract and obligations, the branch skeleton, callers (with result used/ignored), in-repository and external callees, types in the signature, locks it takes, tests that reach it, and its recent git history (fixes marked). `target` is a function name or file:line; a type name returns its hierarchy and header blast radius. Use before reading or editing unfamiliar code instead of opening several files.

params.name: target
params.description: Function name (`Router::process_packet`) or `file:line` inside it.

params.name: max_chars
params.description: Character budget for the whole pack (2000-12000).

tools.name: get_upstream_callers
tools.description: Finds every call site of a function/method across the repository (GNU Global reference index; falls back to ripgrep when the index is unavailable). Each hit shows file:line, the enclosing caller function, the call line, and whether the return value is used or ignored. Use after changing a function's signature, return values, error codes, preconditions or side effects to check that callers still hold up.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function or method name, e.g. 'process_packet' (a 'Class::' prefix is accepted and stripped).

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict caller files, e.g. 'src/*'.

tools.name: get_impact
tools.description: Shows everything a change to a function can affect, several levels deep, in one call: its callers, their callers, and so on (or, with direction='callees', everything it calls). Each call site shows file:line, whether the result is used or ignored, and which callers are program entry points, threads/callbacks or tests; virtual methods include their overrides. Use instead of repeated get_upstream_callers when a function's signature, return values, error handling or side effects change and you need the full blast radius.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name, optionally qualified (`Class::method`, `ns::fn`), e.g. 'process_packet'.

params.name: depth
params.description: How many call levels to follow (1-6).

params.name: direction
params.description: 'callers' (who is affected) or 'callees' (what it depends on).

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict results to some files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

tools.name: get_call_paths
tools.description: Finds how one function reaches another: the shortest call chains from `from_symbol` to `to_symbol` (up to 3), with the file:line and source line of every hop, including threads and callbacks started on the way. Use to answer 'how does the RPC handler end up in this code?', 'is this path possible?', or to explain a stack trace.

params.name: from_symbol
params.description: Function the path starts from, e.g. 'main' or an RPC handler.

params.name: to_symbol
params.description: Function the path must reach.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Longest call chain to consider.

tools.name: find_entry_paths
tools.description: Answers 'can outside input reach this code, and how?': walks callers back from a function to program entry points (main, WinMain, DllMain, ServiceMain), thread start routines and registered callbacks, and shows the call chain from each entry with file:line; also lists the tests that reach it. Use when judging the exposure of a risky change (a memcpy, a parser, a new error path) or when code looks unreachable.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name, optionally qualified (`Class::method`, `ns::fn`), e.g. 'process_packet'.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Longest call chain to consider.

tools.name: get_symbol_definition
tools.description: Locates where a C++ symbol (function, method, class, struct, enum, macro, typedef) is defined, including overloads, with kind, signature and file:line (GNU Global; falls back to ripgrep + ctags). Use to jump to the implementation of something referenced in a diff.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Symbol name, e.g. 'zero_copy_allocate' or 'Packet'.

tools.name: get_symbol_contract
tools.description: Shows the contract of a C++ function or type used by the diff: declaration and definition signatures, qualifiers (const, noexcept, virtual, override, static, [[nodiscard]], ...), the leading doc comment, Doxygen tags (@pre, @post, @return, @throws, @warning, @note) and obligation keywords (MUST, NEVER, thread-safe, ownership, non-null). Use to check that changed code honours the requirements of what it calls (e.g. every allocation must be released, pointer must be non-null, lock must be held).

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function or type name, e.g. 'zero_copy_allocate'.

tools.name: get_type_hierarchy
tools.description: Shows a class's place in the inheritance tree: its base classes, every class derived from it (recursively), and each virtual method with the class that introduces it and every override (file:line), from Universal Ctags without compiling. Use before changing a virtual method, a base class or an interface, and to find every implementation behind a call through a base pointer.

params.name: type_name
params.description: Class or struct name, optionally qualified, e.g. 'Transport'.

tools.name: query_graph
tools.description: Answers free-form structural questions over the code graph with a small query language: `callers*2 of process_packet`, `callees of Router::process_packet`, `derived of Transport`, `bases*3 of TlsTransport`, `overrides of send_frame`, `members of Router`, `includers*2 of packet.hpp in src/*`, `definitions of Packet`, `entry-points`. Use when the dedicated tools do not fit the question; depth up to 6.

params.name: query
params.description: Query such as `callers*2 of process_packet in src/*`; relations: callers, callees, derived, bases, overrides, members, includers, definitions; or `entry-points`.

tools.name: track_struct_risks
tools.description: Finds low-level memory operations that depend on the exact layout of a struct/class: sizeof/offsetof, memcpy/memmove/memset/memcmp, reinterpret_cast/C-style casts/bit_cast, raw send/recv/read/write/fwrite/mmap, byte-order conversions, packing pragmas, unions and static_asserts. Checks the matching line and the 2 lines around it, ignores comments, and labels each hit with its risk (wire format, on-disk format, padding, ABI). Use whenever a struct/class gains, loses, reorders or resizes a member.

params.name: struct_name
params.description: Struct/class name, e.g. 'Packet'.

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict files.

tools.name: get_include_blast_radius
tools.description: Lists every C/C++ file that #includes a header (direct consumers), plus files that include it transitively through other headers, grouped by directory with the share of translation units affected. Use when a header changes (macros, inline functions, struct layout, templates, constants) to see which modules must be re-verified and rebuilt.

params.name: header_filename
params.description: Header name or path, e.g. 'packet.hpp' or 'src/net/packet.hpp'.

params.name: transitive_depth
params.description: 1 = direct includers only; 2-3 = also follow headers that include it.

tools.name: track_state_mutations
tools.description: Finds every read/write of a variable or member (assignment, compound assignment, ++/--, mutating method calls) and, for each access, whether a lock (lock_guard, unique_lock, scoped_lock, shared_lock, .lock(), Win32 critical sections and SRW locks, RAII lock wrappers) or std::atomic protects it inside the enclosing function. Flags inconsistent locking (a member written under a mutex in one place and accessed bare in another), which is a likely data race. Use when the diff touches shared state, mutexes or concurrency.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Variable or member name, e.g. 'route_count'.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Optional file (relative path) to restrict the search.

tools.name: track_lock_order
tools.description: Finds potential deadlocks: builds the lock-acquisition order of the whole repository (which lock is taken while another is held, inside each function and through one level of calls) and reports cycles where two code paths take the same locks in opposite orders, the same non-recursive lock taken twice, and locks held across blocking calls (send/recv, file I/O, Sleep, WaitForSingleObject). Recognises std guards (lock_guard, unique_lock, scoped_lock, shared_lock), .lock(), std::lock, Win32 critical sections and SRW locks, and RAII lock wrappers. Use when the diff adds or reorders locks, calls into locking code while holding a lock, or when investigating hangs.

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict the scanned files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Optional lock (mutex/critical section) name to focus on, e.g. 'route_mutex'.

tools.name: get_lock_graph
tools.description: Maps the locks of a subsystem: every lock, the functions that take it, and which lock is taken while another is held, drawn as a small Mermaid diagram plus a table. Use to understand a module's locking design before adding or reordering locks; use track_lock_order to find problems (cycles, locks held across blocking calls).

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict the scanned files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Optional lock (mutex/critical section) name to focus on, e.g. 'route_mutex'.

tools.name: run_file_static_audit
tools.description: Runs cppcheck (no compilation, best-effort includes) on one C/C++ file and returns findings sorted by severity: memory/resource leaks, null dereferences, out-of-bounds, uninitialised variables, use-after-free, bad casts, performance and portability issues. Findings on lines changed in the current diff are marked. Use on every modified .cpp/.c file during review.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path relative to the workspace root.

params.name: only_changed_lines
params.description: If true, keep only findings on changed lines or inside changed functions.

params.name: base_ref
params.description: Git ref used to determine changed lines (empty = default merge-base).

tools.name: find_switch_coverage
tools.description: Checks every `switch` over an enum against the enum's values: lists each switch (file:line, function) and the values it does not handle, and whether a `default:` catches them. Use when an enum gains, loses or renames a value, the classic 'added a value, forgot a case' bug.

params.name: enum_name
params.description: Enum name, optionally qualified, e.g. 'MsgType'.

tools.name: find_counterparts
tools.description: Finds code that should change together with a function: its naming pair (encode/decode, serialize/deserialize, open/close, register/unregister, acquire/release, ...), platform or #ifdef twins (the same function in *_win / *_posix files), and files that historically change together with its file (git). When the function is changed in the current diff, flags the counterparts that were not. Use to catch half-done changes.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name, optionally qualified (`Class::method`, `ns::fn`), e.g. 'process_packet'.

tools.name: find_related_tests
tools.description: Lists the tests that exercise a function: test functions (in test folders or test files, including gtest/Catch/Boost TEST macros) that reach it through calls within `depth` levels, plus test files that mention it. Reports when no test covers it. Use to know which tests to run or update after a change, and whether a new test is needed.

params.name: symbol
params.description: Function name, optionally qualified (`Class::method`, `ns::fn`), e.g. 'process_packet'.

params.name: depth
params.description: How many call levels to follow (1-6).

tools.name: get_line_history
tools.description: Explains why lines look the way they do and whether they were fixed before: git blame per line (ignoring whitespace and moved/copied code) and every commit that changed the range, with bug-fix and revert commits marked 🐞. Use on lines a diff changes or removes, to catch changes that undo an earlier fix, and to find who-changed-what context for a review. No author names are shown.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path relative to the repository root, e.g. 'src/router.cpp'.

params.name: start_line
params.description: First line of the range (1-based).

params.name: end_line
params.description: Last line of the range; 0 means start_line only.

tools.name: get_change_hotspots
tools.description: Ranks the C/C++ files that deserve the closest review: how often they changed (git history up to HEAD), how many of those changes were bug fixes or reverts, how many lines changed, and how many calls come in from other files (code graph). Use to decide where to look hardest in a large diff, or to find fragile areas of an unfamiliar codebase.

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict results to some files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

params.name: since_days
params.description: How far back to look in git history, in days, counted back from the HEAD commit.

tools.name: find_log_origin
tools.description: Finds the code that produced a log or error message: paste the line from a log, crash report or incident, and it strips the variable parts (numbers, hex, GUIDs, quoted values, paths), searches the remaining literal text inside C/C++ string literals, and returns the best-matching format strings with their function and callers. Use to start an investigation from a symptom.

params.name: text
params.description: A log line or error message as it appears in the log; variable parts are removed automatically.

tools.name: verify_finding
tools.description: Re-checks one finding reported earlier by a StaticSight tool (IDs like `F1a2b3c` appear next to leaks, cppcheck errors, ignored results, lock-order cycles, unlocked accesses, switch gaps and unchanged counterparts). Re-runs the tool that produced it on the current code and says whether the finding is reproduced, moved or gone, shows the code around it, and lists what would prove it wrong. Use before putting a finding in a review, and after a fix to confirm it is gone.

params.name: finding_id
params.description: Finding ID shown next to a finding, e.g. 'F1a2b3c'.

tools.name: get_more
tools.description: Returns the next page of a list that another StaticSight tool truncated. Truncated lists end with a note like `…and 42 more call sites. Next: get_more("P1a2b3c")`; pass that token to see the following items (and a new token if there are still more). Use when the first page was not enough to finish the analysis, instead of re-running the tool with a narrower filter.

params.name: token
params.description: Continuation token from a truncated list, e.g. 'P1a2b3c'.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Finds code by MEANING, not exact text, across the whole repository (every language: C/C++, Python, scripts, docs, configs). Use when you know WHAT the code does but not what it is called, e.g. 'where do we retry failed connections?', 'code that parses the packet header', 'where is the registry key written'. Combines a local code-embedding model with keyword matching and returns ranked functions/classes/sections with file:line, score and a short excerpt. Before searching, the local index is refreshed automatically when files changed (large changes refresh in the background; the result says so). After a git pull or big edits you may call refresh_semantic_index first.

params.name: query
params.description: Natural-language description of the code you are looking for (identifiers may be included).

params.name: path_glob
params.description: Optional fnmatch glob to restrict files, e.g. 'src/net/*'.

params.name: language
params.description: Optional language filter, e.g. 'cpp', 'c', 'python', 'markdown', 'yaml'.

params.name: kind
params.description: Optional chunk kind filter, e.g. 'function', 'class', 'section'.

params.name: top_k
params.description: Maximum number of results (1-30).

tools.name: find_similar_code
tools.description: Finds code elsewhere in the repository that is semantically similar to a given region: copy-paste twins, parallel implementations (Windows/Linux variants, encode/decode pairs) and places that probably need the same fix. Use during review when a function or bug fix changed: 'where else do we do this?'. Give a file and line (the enclosing function is used) or an explicit line range.

params.name: file_path
params.description: Path relative to the workspace root.

params.name: start_line
params.description: 1-based line; alone, the enclosing function/chunk is used.

params.name: end_line
params.description: 1-based inclusive end line for an explicit range (optional).

params.name: top_k
params.description: Maximum number of similar regions (1-30).

tools.name: refresh_semantic_index
tools.description: Builds or refreshes the local semantic search index for the workspace (incremental: only files whose content changed are re-embedded). Call it after a git pull, branch switch or large edits, or when semantic_search reports a stale index. Small refreshes finish before returning; large ones continue in the background (check get_index_status). Writes only to StaticSight's own data folder (`.staticsight/` in the repository, ignored by git), never to source files.

params.name: full
params.description: Rebuild from scratch instead of refreshing incrementally.

tools.name: get_index_status
tools.description: Reports the state of the GNU Global symbol index, the semantic search index and the code graph (building with progress, ready, stale, not built), their locations and age, the embedding model, and which CLI engines are installed. Use when caller/definition results say they came from the ripgrep fallback, or to follow a background semantic index build.

prompts.name: review_cpp_changes
prompts.description: Step-by-step workflow for a thorough, evidence-based review of C++ changes using StaticSight tools.

args.name: focus
args.description: Optional area to pay special attention to, e.g. 'locking' or 'the wire format'.

prompts.name: investigate_hang
prompts.description: Workflow to find the cause of a hang, deadlock or stall: lock graph, lock-order cycles, locks held across blocking calls, and the threads involved.

args.name: symptom
args.description: Optional description of the hang or a log line from it.

prompts.name: investigate_incident
prompts.description: Workflow to go from a log line or error message to the root cause: origin of the message, how input reaches it, recent changes, and where else the bug exists.

args.name: log_text
args.description: The log or error line from the incident.

prompts.name: plan_refactor
prompts.description: Workflow to plan a refactor before editing: every place to change, contracts to keep, tests to run, and a step-by-step plan that keeps the code working.

args.name: symbol
args.description: The function or type to change.

args.name: change
args.description: What should change, e.g. 'add a timeout parameter'.

prompts.name: onboard_me
prompts.description: Workflow to understand an unfamiliar area of the code base: main types, entry points and flow, threads and locks, fragile spots and tests.

args.name: area
args.description: The area to learn, e.g. 'the packet router' or 'src/net'.
